summary: This article explains how sea stars, which are not really fish, move on tube feet, eat clams with their stomachs, regrow lost arms, and survive the tides on rocky shores.
introduce: Show the title “Sea Stars of the Shore” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: an animal that hunts and eats other animals
a sea animal with no backbone and a body built around a center, such as a sea urchin
the pull that makes something stick when air or water is pushed out

challengeTerms.def: to grow again a body part that was lost or damaged
all the living things in an area and the way they depend on one another and their surroundings

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that sea stars are among the most amazing animals in the ocean? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a sea star's body helps it survive on a rocky shore.
struggling: Pre-teach predator, echinoderm, and suction with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses invertebrate, regenerate, and ecosystem to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
